To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the BEVI is a valid and reliable measure of international, multicultural and transformative learning, (b) the BEVI can be used to identify the learning processes and outcomes of global education, (c) global education has positive impacts on student learning, (d) global education is a complex and multi-faceted process, (e) global education is an ongoing process of change and development, (f) global education is not a one-time event, (g) global education is
international, multicultural, transformative learning, and global education can be defined, measured, and improved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: How do students’ international experiences influence their personal development and global perspectives?

the following question: What do we know about the processes and outcomes associated with international, multicultural, transformative learning, and how might we apply this knowledge to the design of curricular and co-curricular programs in colleges and universities?
the ways that students learn to be global citizens in a variety of educational settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
global education has become an increasingly prominent feature of colleges and universities in the United States.
the BEVI has been a useful tool for understanding the nature and impact of international, multicultural and transformative learning.
the Forum-BEVS Project provides an array of implications for international, multicultural, transformative learning, and global citizenship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Forum-BEBI Project found that global education is a powerful force for change, but that the field is still struggling to define and measure its impact.

we found that the BEVI was a valuable instrument in assessing global education and that the BEVI results were highly consistent with other measures of global learning, including student self-reports and student reflections, and with other measures of student learning and development, including the Collegiate Learning Assessment (CLA).
the Forum-BEVS Project was a collaborative, cross-cultural effort among a diverse group of faculty and staff from a number of institutions to examine how students develop as global citizens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global education can be a powerful force for social transformation and positive change.
assessment can be a powerful tool for understanding and improving the global education experience for students and institutions alike.
the Forum-BEVS Project offers a set of implications and applications for the design and implementation of assessment in international, multicultural, transformative learning.
